title: Waste, Pollution & the Environment
whatItIs: Construction can pollute air, water and land. You must not cause or allow pollution, and anyone who produces or handles waste has a legal duty of care for it.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT cause or allow pollution of the air, water or ground.
Contaminated water MUST NOT go into surface water drains.
Waste MUST only go to someone authorised to take it.
Hazardous and non-hazardous waste MUST be stored separately.

keyFacts: Pollution entering, or about to enter, water or the ground? Call the pollution hotline at once.

onTheTest.question: Where can water from washing out a concrete mixer go?
options: Into the nearest surface water drain
Down a drain with a blue manhole cover
Onto open ground to soak away
onTheTest.why: Contaminated water must not go into surface water drains or the ground. Collect it for reuse or treatment, or use a registered waste carrier.

onTheTest.question: A man offers to take your site waste away cheaply. What must you check first?
options: That he's authorised to take waste
That his van is big enough
That he can take it today
That he'll give you a receipt
onTheTest.why: Waste duty of care: only transfer waste to an authorised person, eg a registered carrier. Check the public register.

traps: Blue manhole cover = surface water: never put anything but clean water down it.
Concrete slurry and detergents pollute too, not just oil and chemicals.
Your duty of care doesn't end at the gate: check where the waste is going.
